patch.value: Failed atomic create compensation erases orphan reconciliation markers

Greptile's exact-head review of PR 73 found that compensateCreate removed csv-tx and csv-txrow ownership markers before attempting pm close. If close then failed, the item remained open but could no longer be located by transaction id. Close first, preserve markers on any failed close, clean markers only after confirmed terminal state, and make the public atomic contract disclose best-effort compensation and reconciliation.

A red regression proves failed close preserves both transaction markers; Compensation closes before removing markers; A marker-cleanup failure is logged and leaves a closed marked item discoverable; Public README, option type, example, and flag describe best-effort compensation, intentionally non-reverted pre-existing updates, and inspect-and-reconcile guidance; npm run release:check passes exact 100/100/100/100 coverage and every repository quality gate
Create a transaction-marked item, force pm close to fail, call compensateCreate, then inspect the still-open item tags.
A failed close leaves the open item transaction-marked and discoverable; successful or already-closed compensation removes the markers; public docs require reconciliation.
The old implementation stripped both markers before close, so a close failure left an unmarked open orphan while README and API text promised complete create compensation.
